explanation: A Spanish saying warns against marrying or setting sail on a Tuesday. In Italy the unlucky date is traditionally Friday the 17th, whose numeral XVII can be rearranged as VIXI, Latin for 'I have lived'.

claims.text: In Spain and much of Latin America, Tuesday the 13th (martes 13) is traditionally considered an unlucky day.
A Spanish proverb warns against marrying or setting sail on a Tuesday ('En martes, ni te cases ni te embarques').
In Italy, Friday the 17th is traditionally considered unlucky.
The Roman numeral XVII can be rearranged as VIXI, Latin for 'I have lived', a phrase associated with death.

evidence.summaryExcerpt: The vixi link is the leading explanation for the superstition, but it is a hypothesis. Wikipedia says it has been suggested that the Romans found the number 17 disturbing because of this anagram. Another source calls it perhaps because in Roman numerals 17 is written XVII, which can be rearranged to VIXI, and notes that vixi can be a euphemism for "I am dead."
